item.title: Jupiter Lend Under Stress: Analyzing the October 10 Liquidation Event
item.description:
On October 10, 2025, U.S. President Donald Trump announced that the U.S. would impose an additional 100% tariff on Chinese imports. This announcement was followed by a rapid market selloff: over the course of October 10, the price of ETH fell as much as 12% and SOL fell as much as 24%.

The wave of selling ultimately triggered $19B in liquidations across derivative markets. But how did this affect other venues that offer leverage, like credit markets?

item.title: Building an Agentic Pipeline for Onchain Data Analysis
item.description:
At Blocmates, we used Claude to help us write SQL queries and Python scripts for data analysis. This helped us finish research reports faster, but it also introduced another problem: managing context.

Each new analysis required us to provide Claude with table schemas, API documentation, and other project-specific information. We also had to copy and paste code between Claude, Dune, and other tools. These repetitive tasks took time and introduced opportunities for errors– undermining the time saved by using an LLM in the first place.

item.title: Building a Local AI System for Financial Markets & Digital Asset Intelligence
item.description:
Financial markets generate an enormous amount of information every day, from macroeconomic developments to digital asset markets and protocol governance. In the past, I’ve struggled to keep up with these developments while writing research reports.

So to streamline my research process, I built a locally hosted AI system that aggregates news and market data, identifies important developments, and generates daily research briefings. Using locally hosted large language models (LLMs), the system has reduced my daily news intake from 1–2 hours to approximately 20 minutes.

item.title: Reverse-Engineering Jupiter Lend Liquidations: Part 2
item.description:
In Part 1, we identified Jupiter Lend’s liquidation instructions, mapped their account arguments, and decoded the raw amounts of debt repaid and collateral seized.

In this walkthrough, we’ll combine those findings into a single DuneSQL query using common table expressions (CTEs). The query reconstructs liquidation records from raw instructions and joins Dune’s prices.hour table to calculate the USD value of debt repaid and collateral seized.

We’ll work through the query in four phases, following how each CTE transforms and passes data to the next. Select a CTE in the interactive query below to explore its role in building the final dataset.

item.title: Reverse-Engineering Jupiter Lend Liquidations: Part 1
item.description: How do you analyze activity on a blockchain protocol when there's no ready-made dataset? In this guide, I demonstrate how to write SQL queries in Dune and use Solscan to reverse-engineer Solana program instructions, using Jupiter Lend liquidations as a practical example.
